The bar was written before measuring (3 of 4 improving AND median past +0.03) and it is met 4/4 at 4.5x the required median. Across all six seeds ever run at each width the medians are 192x3 +0.2046 and 256x3 +0.3197.

Not a leverage artefact: average exposure is essentially unchanged (6.80% -> 7.02%), so this is a better forecaster rather than a book putting more money on the table. Worst drawdown rose 21.4% -> 22.6% and that is reported, not buried - the operator's balance criterion says a gain merely PROPORTIONAL to its extra drawdown is not worth taking, and +0.13 of score for 1.2 points of drawdown is disproportionate in the candidate's favour.

P39's inconclusive verdict is vindicated rather than overturned: 256 really does pay, and the two-seed mean that happened to point the same way was still not evidence. The right call was to reseed, and reseeding produced a result that does not depend on which draws we happened to take.

SEPARATE CORRECTION, and it cuts against us: the published promotion bar of +0.2550 was derived from two seeds of the 192x3 genome. Over all six seeds that genome reproduces at +0.2046. The bar was measured on a lucky pair and is optimistic by about 0.05 - the fourth appearance of selection optimism in this ledger. P47 compares against both numbers and prints them side by side.

NOT YET A CHAMPION. This is a research-score win on held-out selection; the sealed 2026 readout has not been opened and was not an input to any of it. P47 does the single build and the single readout.

why:
The operator's instruction, stated as an experiment: what matters is the SUCCESS RATE of a trade, and fewer-but-larger is acceptable if each one is better. Three instruments already say the book's edge lives in its very top convictions - fit_diagnosis (77% precision above 0.75), P42 (lowering the bar loses monotonically) and P44 (spreading wider loses at matched exposure). None of them tested the OPPOSITE direction: raising the bar and paying for the lost breadth with size.

P42 walked the bar DOWN (0.70/0.65/0.60, all worse). This walks it UP and compensates, so exposure stays comparable and the arm isolates trade QUALITY instead of quietly testing 'hold less'. That compensation is the lesson P44 taught at its own expense: a lever that is a denominator of sizing moves two quantities.
judge: Score first, then the trade ledger: the point is a HIGHER hit rate per trade, so report win rate and average trade alongside the score, not just the total. The uncompensated arm is there to separate 'better trades' from 'less exposure' - if the compensated arm wins and the uncompensated one does not, size is doing the work and the finding is about sizing, not selection. Drawdown reported either way: concentrating into fewer, larger positions is more tail risk, and that is the operator's call to make, not mine.
verdict: baseline: +0.0000; bar 0.80 + size up: -0.0553; bar 0.85 + size up: -0.0836; bar 0.80 [uncompensated]: -0.0534; ceiling 0.70 [CONTROL]: +0.0990 (DEEP dd 24.8%)
result:
REFUTED in both halves, and the way it fails is more useful than a win would have been.

  arm                          delta    77101    77102   exposure   maxDD
  baseline                   +0.0000   0.3533   0.1567      6.55%   19.2%
  bar 0.80 + size up         -0.0553   0.2684   0.1310      6.23%   19.4%
  bar 0.85 + size up         -0.0836   0.2298   0.1130      5.57%   19.1%
  bar 0.80 [uncompensated]   -0.0534   0.2695   0.1337      6.15%   19.1%
  ceiling 0.70 [CONTROL]     +0.0990   0.4976   0.2103      7.84%   24.8%

Every arm loses, both seeds, monotonically in the height of the bar. Eight and five times the ~0.01 noise floor, so this is not a draw.

THE READING IS IN THE PAIR, not in the losses. The compensated arm loses -0.0553 and the uncompensated one -0.0534. The difference between them is 0.0019 - INSIDE the noise floor. Size compensation, which was the whole mechanism of the hypothesis, did nothing measurable. The judge asked exactly this question in advance: if the compensated arm wins and the uncompensated one does not, the finding is about sizing. It came back the other way, so the loss is pure SELECTION: the trades living between conviction 0.75 and 0.80 are, on net, profitable, and refusing them refuses profit. Paying for them with a bigger stake on what remains does not buy them back.

Set beside P42, which walked the same bar DOWN (0.70, 0.65, 0.60 - all worse, monotonically), the entry bar at 0.75 is now measured as an INTERIOR OPTIMUM: it loses in both directions, with size held constant and with size compensating. Three experiments have now pushed on this lever from three angles and it does not move. The entry bar is finished as a source of improvement, and that is worth more than another inconclusive nudge - it closes a road instead of leaving it half-walked.

THE CONTROL DID ITS JOB AND IS NOT A PROPOSAL. regime_deploy 0.70 gains +0.0990, which proves the harness engages and the losses above are real rather than an arm that never fired. It is not an adoption candidate: exposure rises 6.55% -> 7.84% and worst drawdown 19.2% -> 24.8%. Score +39% relative for drawdown +29% relative is gain PROPORTIONAL to risk, which under the operator's balance criterion means prefer the smaller drawdown. It buys nothing; it only puts more money on the same edge.

WHERE THIS POINTS. The operator's underlying instinct - fewer trades, better ones - is not refuted; only the crudest instrument for it is. Raising a single global threshold does not select better trades, it selects FEWER of the same trades. Choosing better ones needs a rule that is conditional on the state of the market rather than a constant, which is what the trade ledger already found the material for: the rules separating winners from losers are conjunctions (trend_dist, ret_16, body_prev), and the strongest of them carries a +0.41 lift on the base rate. That is A73's territory and it is where the next experiment goes.

gate_forensics (2026-09-04) settled what 2025 actually is. The model is not quiet in 2025 - it produces 111,887 signals above the entry bar, essentially the same raw material as 2024's 112,935, a year that returned +155.7%. What differs is what survives the gates:

  2024     112,935        579      324   +155.7%
  2025     111,887        163       75     -3.0%

Same opinions, a quarter of the survivors. And the funnel names the gate. Vetoes as a share of the signals that cleared the bar, weak years against the ones that paid:

  regime     65.4% vs 40.5%   +24.9 points
  crowd      37.8% vs 18.1%   +19.7 points
  oracle-nn  68.3% vs 52.7%   +15.7 points
  meta       31.4% vs 33.7%    -2.3 points   <- not involved

The aggregate blurs two different diseases, and 2025 alone is the one that matters here. Against the average of the paying years, 2025's gates read: crowd 18.1% vs 18.1% (IDENTICAL - the fear floor is not what shuts 2025 down, that is 2022's story), meta 39.3% vs 33.7%, oracle-nn 60.4% vs 52.7%, and regime 52.9% vs 40.5%. One gate stands clear of the rest.

`regime` veto is `breadth_gate` and nothing else: when breadth falls under 0.30 the module vetoes EVERY entry and demands the whole book to cash. It is an absolute switch, not a scaling. So for over half of 2025 the system was ordered flat, in a year whose perfect-hindsight ceiling was +21,958%.

Nothing here is capacity: book_full is 43 for the whole year, and no_consensus is 0 in every year (consensus_k = 1, so that filter is inert everywhere - worth knowing on its own). Nor is it sizing: average deployment is 28.1% against the paying years' 32%, a difference far too small to turn +155% into -3%.

This walks breadth_gate down. It is CHEAP - a risk lever, no retraining - which is the whole dividend of diagnosing first: the measurement cost four minutes and the experiment it aims costs one paired run instead of the three that P42, P44 and P46 spent guessing.
judge:
SCORED ON THE CONSISTENCY LAW, worst calendar year + 0.10*CAGR over 2018-2025. That metric is the one that makes this test honest, because breadth_gate EARNS ITS KEEP IN THE CRASHES: it exists to empty the book in a broad bear, and 2018 and 2022 are broad bears. An arm that rescues 2025 by handing back more than it gains in 2018/2022 must read as a loss, and the worst-year term is what enforces that. Total return alone would hide it.

REPORT PER YEAR, NOT ONLY THE SCORE. The whole point is which years moved. An arm that lifts 2025 and drops 2018 is a different finding from one that lifts both, and the score alone cannot tell them apart.

DRAWDOWN TRAVELS WITH EVERY NUMBER. Removing a risk-off switch is removing a brake; the balance criterion applies, so a gain merely proportional to the extra drawdown is not worth taking and the operator decides, not me.

KILL: if every arm loses on the consistency score, breadth_gate at 0.30 is correct as it stands and the 2025 answer is not in this lever. The next place to look is then the oracle-nn trend veto (60.4% vs 52.7%), which needs a retrain and is therefore the expensive branch - taken only if this cheap one dies.

EXPECTED, written before the run so it can be wrong: the 0.20 arm gains and the OFF arm loses, because the gate is doing real work in 2018/2022 and the question is whether 0.30 is too eager rather than whether the idea is wrong. If OFF wins outright I have misunderstood what the gate is for and will say so.

The operator's balance criterion is stated for the opposite case - a gain merely proportional to its extra drawdown is not worth taking - and applied in mirror it reads clearly: the incumbent's extra 26% of return costs 72% more drawdown. That is a disproportionately expensive advantage. But the criterion is the operator's to apply, not mine, and the stated success test is the forward RETURN, which this does not beat. Recorded as not adopted.

WHAT SURVIVED SCRUTINY, because the headline is the least interesting part:

  - It transfers in time. Fitted on 2018-2023 with 2024-2025 never shown to the sampler; holdout score +0.1028 against the incumbent's +0.0280.
  - It is not a lucky point. 57 of 87 trials beat the incumbent on the held-out half; the top-20 region median holdout is +0.115 at a median drawdown of 18.8%, BELOW the incumbent's 20.8%.
  - It is not leverage. Average exposure 6.75% -> 7.25%, and per year it goes DOWN in six of eight while returns rise in all of them. Same stake per name (0.1667/3 = 0.0556 against 0.15/2 = 0.075), spread wider.
  - It transfers across NETS. Run against three nets it was never tuned on it wins 3/3, including prev_champion_64ch, a different architecture: +0.2451 there, +0.0531 on _candidate, +0.0397 on the fresh 256x3. So it is not co-adapted to one export's calibration - the failure the held-out years could not have caught.

AND IT SETTLES THE METHOD QUESTION THE OPERATOR RAISED. Eight of the twelve live thresholds had never been searched at all, and no interaction between any two had ever been tested. The joint optimum picks max_positions 3 with position_fraction raised to hold the per-name stake - which is precisely the combination P44 could not test, and whose absence P44's own writeup recorded as a confound. Every single-lever refutation in this ledger that touches a denominator of sizing is now unproven rather than closed.
